plan.notes: Source: official QCC program page (Associate in Science) at https://www.qcc.edu/computer-and-information-technology/computer-science-transfer; term-by-term sequence transcribed from the page's official 'Curriculum' program-grid table (Course Title / Course # / Semester Offered / Credits / Prerequisites) on 2026-09-30. QCC program pages do not print a catalog year; the page reflects the current 2026-2027 curriculum as of the transcription date. Transcription method: fetched official page HTML and extracted the curriculum table cells verbatim (course codes, titles, credits, prerequisites); nothing invented. Total credits required per the grid's own published total: 60 (semester totals 15+15+16+14), which matches the 60-credit degree minimum stated in QCC's transfer articulations — no discrepancy. Program Code CS. Caveats: (1) Semesters 1-2 each offer an either/or OR choice (CSC 108 Computer Science I OR ROS 108 Introduction to Robotics; CSC 109 Computer Science II OR ROS 109 Intermediate Robotics), encoded as choice slots per schema; the ROS alternative is not eligible for transfer credit to WPI per the page's transfer note. (2) QCC requires a grade of 'C' or higher in CSC 108/CSC 109/ROS 108/ROS 109 for the CSC 211/208/212 prerequisite chains; prereq codes point at the choice-slot codes per validator rules. (3) Placement prerequisites (college-level English placement; MAT 100 or appropriate placement for CSC 108; MAT 124 or appropriate placement for MAT 233; MAT 123 or appropriate placement for MAT 125) are placement/assessment requirements, not courses; program admissions additionally require placement into college-level English and MAT 100 with C or higher or appropriate placement. (4) AP Computer Science A exam score of 3+ may substitute for the CSC 101 prerequisite of CSC 108. (5) Lab Science, Humanities, and Social Science electives are student-choice electives given distinct placeholder codes because QCC does not print specific course numbers for them. (6) CSC 212 Introduction to Software Engineering is the program capstone (student or instructor-chosen project).
